findings.quote: Super admins who are not members also get 404 here — they use `/admin`; document this in a code comment (proposed change is listed in HANDOFF, not built).
findings.problem: G5's 2.1 (the step this one extends) already decided the opposite: `my_context()` (G2 1.3b) returns EVERY org for super admins with `membership_status = null`, `requireOrgMember` accepts `isSuperAdmin` with `membershipStatus = null`, and the org shell shows a 'Viewing as super admin' banner, precisely so the founder can trial the whole web app as super admin (the stated primary objective). 3.1 as written instructs the agent to revert that: `find orgs entry with … membership_status = 'active' … Not found → notFound()` gives super admins a 404, the HANDOFF Finish item records 'super admins are not org members (404 on /o/<slug> unless invited)', done_when #2 and #9, notes and open_issues #1 repeat it. Two agents following 2.1 and 3.1 produce incompatible guards, and the founder cannot open `/o/<slug>/*` after 2.5.
findings.fix: In Build 1 replace the quoted sentence and the membership rule with: 'Keep 2.1's rule: the entry must have `membership_status = 'active'`, OR `is_super_admin` is true and the entry has `membership_status = null` (my_context returns every org for super admins). Non-super users with a missing, `pending` or `disabled` entry get `notFound()`. For super admins `hasPerm`/`hasAnyPerm` return true (mirrors `app.has_perm`; confirm in `9999_init.sql`) so `requirePerm` passes; `OrgShell` keeps 2.1's "Viewing as super admin" banner; `OrgSwitcher` lists active memberships plus, for super admins, the current org and a link to `/admin`.' Delete the 404-for-super-admin sentences from Finish (HANDOFF note), done_when #2 ('404 for unknown slug, non-member, pending or disabled membership' → add 'except super admins, who pass with membershipStatus null'), done_when #9, notes, and open_issues #1 (resolved by G2/G5; G5's 2.2 already tells 2.5 to add the founder as first admin only as an option).

findings.quote: if `require-org.ts` already exports `requireOrgMember(slug)` and `require-perm.ts` exports `requirePerm(ctx, perm)`, extend them; if they are stubs, complete them with the signatures below.
findings.problem: G5's 2.1 ships them fully, not as stubs, with a fixed shape: `requireOrgMember(slug)` → `OrgContext = {org: {orgId, slug, name, status}, membershipStatus, personId, householdId, permissions: PermissionKey[], isSuperAdmin}`, `requireWritable(ctx)` (throws `organization_suspended` when status = 'suspended'), `hasPerm`/`hasAnyPerm`/`requirePerm(ctx, perm)` → `forbidden()` with `experimental.authInterrupts` already set, `getAuthContext()` in `src/lib/auth/context.ts`, plus `toActionError`/`ActionResult` for Server Action returns. 3.1 then defines a different shape (`org: {org_id, …}`, `writable` field), re-instructs setting `authInterrupts` and an `error.tsx` fallback, and uses `ctx.org.org_id` in Build 4. An agent following 3.1 literally rewrites 2.1's guards and breaks 2.2's `/admin` code.
findings.fix: Rewrite Build 1 to: 'These files exist from 2.1 with exactly this shape: … (paste the G5 shape). Change only: (a) `requirePerm(ctx, perm | perms[])` — an array means any-of; (b) add `isWritable(ctx)` (= status in trial/active/past_due) next to `requireWritable` (or a derived `writable` getter) — do not rename fields; (c) add `app/(org)/o/[orgSlug]/{not-found,forbidden}.tsx` if 2.1 did not. Use `ctx.org.orgId` everywhere, `toActionError`/`ActionResult` for every Server Action result, and 2.1's 403 mechanism as recorded in HANDOFF (do not add an `error.tsx` fallback unless HANDOFF says `forbidden()` failed).' Update Inputs bullet 1 and open_issues #2/#4 accordingly.

findings.problem: 2.2's Admins tab (G5) can only disable/enable a membership or grant it all 12 permissions; it cannot remove a single permission. The per-permission grid arrives in 3.2. The manual check cannot be followed as written.
findings.fix: Replace with: 'in the Supabase SQL Editor run `delete from public.org_membership_permissions where membership_id = '<id>' and permission = 'org.settings';` (find the id in `/admin/churches/[orgId]` Admins tab or `select id from public.org_memberships where …`) → `/o/<slug>/settings` → 403 and Settings hidden from the nav; restore with `insert into public.org_membership_permissions (membership_id, permission) values ('<id>', 'org.settings');` (or use the Admins tab "grant all"). Test with a second, non-super account — a super admin passes every permission check.'

findings.quote: (c) success → `confirmLogoUpload(orgSlug, path)` re-checks the object via `storage.from('org-assets').list('<org_id>/logo')`
findings.problem: Reads on `storage.objects` go through `ca_storage_select` → `app.can_read_object`, which for `org-assets` is true only when the org appears in `org_directory_info`; that is fine for members, but `list()` also depends on the `storage.foldername`/prefix search which the local shim only approximates and which some Supabase versions gate differently from `createSignedUrl`. More importantly the DESIGN §7 path template is `{org_id}/logo/{uuid}.png` and G4 reports a `logo_path` check expression copied from `9999_init.sql`; if 1.2's check pins the extension (or the `{org_id}/logo/` prefix), a `.jpg`/`.webp` `prepareLogoUpload` fails at the DB before the upload with SQLSTATE 23514 and the UI shows a confusing check error.
findings.fix: Add to Build 4 Logo: 'Read the `organization_settings.logo_path` check constraint in `9999_init.sql` first; accept client-side only the extensions/prefix it allows (if it forces `.png`, offer PNG only and say so in the helper text). Confirm the upload with `createSignedUrl(path, 60)` (a 200 proves the object exists) instead of `list()`; map a 23514 from `prepareLogoUpload` to "Unsupported file name" rather than a generic error.'

findings.quote: "Published sermons", "Active announcements", "Current bulletin" counts (`sermons`, `announcements`, `bulletins` with `publish_at <= now()`; RLS limits rows)
findings.problem: `bulletins` carry `starts_on`/`ends_on` (check `ends_on >= starts_on`) plus `publish_at default now()`; 'current' by `publish_at` alone counts every bulletin ever uploaded. 'Active announcements' also ignores `expires_at`.
findings.fix: Replace with: '"Published sermons" = `publish_at <= now()`; "Active announcements" = `publish_at <= now() and (expires_at is null or expires_at > now())`; "Current bulletin" = the bulletin with `publish_at <= now() and starts_on <= today and ends_on >= today` (today in the org timezone via `@church/domain/dates.ts`), else "No bulletin for this week".'
